anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Application-level SQL or transaction design causes the engine to process more data or keep transactions open longer than business logic requires.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly: Concurrent transactions compete for incompatible locks on the same resources, producing blocking chains or deadlocks in the lock manager.

Combined phenomena: Inefficient, long-running statements hold extensive row, page, or table locks while other sessions attempt conflicting operations. The system exhibits extreme and erratic statement latencies, soaring lock-wait time, frequent deadlock victim errors, swelling connection-pool queues, and application timeouts. Monitoring views show the same heavyweight SQL text both in slow-query logs and at the head of long blocker trees; lock-wait graphs grow deeper, and throughput collapses despite low CPU utilization as sessions idle in lock waits.

Causal chain: Over-broad scans, missing predicates, or transactions stretched across user think-time enlarge the lock footprint and duration of each unit of work. This increases the probability that concurrent requests target already-held rows or keys, triggering lock waits. The resulting contention further prolongs the problematic transactions, which in turn extends their lock hold times—a positive feedback loop that intensifies blocking and deadlocks. Thus, flawed workload logic and lock contention reinforce each other, jointly degrading OLTP performance far more severely than either issue alone.

entry.official_definition: Maximum wait for connection, in seconds; zero or not specified means wait indefinitely.
entry.trigger_condition: A libpq client connection attempt exceeds connect_timeout seconds.
entry.workload_impact: The client connection attempt fails instead of waiting indefinitely.
entry.default_behavior: Zero or absent value means wait indefinitely.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
